claim: Heights compute the transfer. (1) Corner matchings: in a point split of a plane knot space with Kasteleyn signs, choosing for each line one corner, with each face receiving exactly one, is a bijection with the solutions up to complement. The three port lines have two corners in the merged face, so the line-face graph has double edges; HANDLE-LOCALITY A's matching statement is to be read with corners as edges. (2) The transfer R(L), the set of (port pattern, L pattern) pairs that occur together, is decided exactly by heights. Fix L's matched corner; the heights are the integer solutions of difference constraints. Their projection onto the regions of the three ports and L's points is cut out by the shortest-path distances between those regions, and a parity vector is feasible iff halving the constraints leaves no negative cycle. A point's value relative to another is the parity of their height difference. This takes polynomial time, with no enumeration. Verified: corner matchings equal the solutions on all 71 point splits of the planar census and 10-point spaces; the transfer by heights equals enumeration on all 1,221 (split, line) pairs of the planar census, five grown and two prism spaces to 14 points.
